  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

The doors to the Council Chamber on the 9th Floor will open at 1:40 p.m. for Open Session. Please be
mindful that seating is limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the Rental Housing Board by sending them to the Rental Housing Board
Secretary at rentalhousingboard@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Rental
Housing Board prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the
meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number and/or subject matter.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 a.m. and
prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact
the Office of the Housing Protection Board at (310) 412-4330 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities
Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation
thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services
in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation,
or service by contacting the Housing Protection Department by telephone at 310-412-4330, FAX at 310-412-
4276, One Manchester Boulevard, Suite 602, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to
rentalhousingboard@cityofinglewood.org no later than 48 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

RENTAL HOUSING BOARD MEMBERS  DEPARTMENT DEPUTY DIRECTOR

   Inglewood, California
  October 8, 2025

The Rental Housing Board of the City of Inglewood, California, held a meeting on
Wednesday, October 8, 2025, in the Council Chambers located in City Hall of said City.

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Chairperson Heaney called
the Rental Housing Board into session at the hour of 2:02 p.m.

The Rental Housing Board Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Chairperson Heaney, Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton,
  Fragoso and Brown; and
  Absent: Rental Housing Board Member Evans.

City officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Qiana Lowe  Housing Protection Deputy Director
  Amari Watson  Rental Housing Board Liaison
  NeCosia James  Rental Housing Board Secretary
  L'Oréal Threat  Rental Housing Board Assistant
  Shatara Smith  Rental Housing Board Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Chairperson Heaney inquired if any
persons were present who wished to address the Rental Housing Board on any item on the
Agenda.

There was no response.

CONFLICT OF INTEREST DECLARATION. It was moved by Chairperson Heaney
and seconded by Rental Housing Board Member Hamilton that a roll call be taken to
confirm there was no conflict of interest with any items on the agenda with the Rental
Housing Board. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, and Chairperson
  Heaney;
Noes: None; and
Absent: Rental Housing Board Member Evans.

The Renal Housing Board Members had no conflicts of interest with any item on the
agenda.

MINUTES – APPROVED. It was moved by Rental Housing Board Member Brown and
seconded by Rental Housing Board Member Hamilton that the Minutes of the Rental
Housing Board Meetings held on February 12, 2025, December 11, 2024, and July 9, 2025
be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
 Ayes:  Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, and Chairperson
  Heaney;
Noes: None; and
Absent: Rental Housing Board Member Evans.

HOUSING PROTECTION LONG-TERM RENTALS DIVISION PRESENTATION
ON CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT. Chairperson Heaney announced a presentation from
the Housing Protection Long-Term Rentals Division by Rental Housing Board Liaison
Watson. Rental Housing Board Secretary James introduced Rental Housing Board Liaison
Watson to provide a presentation on Capital Improvement.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the presentation would provide a
brief overview of the Capital Improvement Petition process. Rental Housing Board Liaison
Watson explained that the presentation would include factors that the Rental Housing
Board should consider when evaluating a Capital Improvement Pass-Through Fee. Rental
Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the presentation will include a proposal for
how Capital Improvement petitions will be presented.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that a capital improvement is an
improvement and/or major rehabilitation of a rental complex that involves more than
ordinary maintenance and repairs. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that
capital improvements must mainly benefit the tenants and be useful for at least five years.
Rental Housing Board Liaison explained that capital improvements must also be
permanently affixed or relatively immovable, and suitable for the intended use of the rental
property. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that major rehabilitations
classified as capital improvements include new roofs, replacing plumbing pipes, and the
creation of new facilities such as recreation rooms or pools.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that capital improvements are not routine
maintenance and repairs, replacements due to lack of maintenance, common facility
upkeep, compliance upgrades for long-standing violations, and coin-operated or fee-based
improvements. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that if a property owner
has been cited by Code Enforcement due to violations, the repairs that a property owner
makes in response will be seen as compliance and not a capital improvement.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that an owner may recover up to 50% of
their Capital Improvement costs. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the
property owner’s improvement cost for a rental unit must be over $5,000 to qualify as a
Capital Improvement. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson then explained that the
property owner’s improvement cost for a property must be over $10,000 to qualify as a
Capital Improvement.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that there are Capital Improvement Pass-
Through Fee limitations of $100 per unit, per month. Rental Housing Board Liaison
Watson explained that a capital Improvement pass-through fee shall not exist for more than

  2
 72 months or allow the owner to recover more than 50% of total costs. Rental Housing
Board Liaison Watson explained that a Capital Improvement Pass-Through Fee does not
apply to new tenants after the petition's filing date, Section 8 tenants, or subsidized units.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that once an owner submits a Capital
Improvement Petition, the Housing Protection Long-Term Rentals Division staff will
determine if the improvement qualifies as a Capital Improvement, if all required permits
were obtained, if the property is currently registered and there are no outstanding fees with
the Housing Protection Long-Term Rentals Division, if there are city violations, and if the
tenant list or rent roll matches the tenancies that are listed in the online Residential Registry
system.

Rental Housing Board Member Hamilton asked if a property owner’s improvement to their
rental property was in response to a Code Enforcement violation, would the improvement
equate to a Capital Improvement.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson responded in the negative and explained that
pursuant to the City of Inglewood’s Housing Protection Ordinance 21-09’s plain language,
the owner’s action to address a city violation would not constitute a capital improvement.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the owner must provide a Letter of
Intent for Capital Improvement Pass-Through Fee to each of the affected tenant(s). Rental
Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that this letter informs the tenants about the
specific improvement and its associated cost for which the landlord has filed a Capital
Improvement Petition.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that in a previous Rental Housing Board
meeting, Capital Improvement Petition submission stipulations were established. Rental
Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that due to the Rental Housing Board’s previous
vote, Capital Improvement Petition submissions will only apply to improvements made
after December 5, 2019. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that Capital
Improvement Petition applications submitted before December 5, 2025 must include all
improvements since December 5, 2019.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that after December 5, 2025, all Capital
Improvement Petitions must be submitted within 12 months of completing the
improvement.

Rental Housing Board Member Brown asked if an owner made multiple capital
improvements from December 2019 and December 2025, would the Capital Improvement
Pass-Through Fee include all capital improvements.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson responded that the Capital Improvement Pass-
Through Fee may have to be calculated together.

  3
 Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the factors to consider when
determining a Capital Improvement Pass-Through fee include the improvement cost, the
total number of units, the current rental amounts, and the dates of the last rent increases.
Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the Rental Housing Board Members
may also want to consider if the tenants are paying higher rent increases due to their unit
qualifying for a Below Market Rent Increase, if the tenants are paying a registration pass-
through fee, and if the tenants received temporary relocation.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson introduced a Capital Improvement sample binder
to show how the capital improvements will be presented to the Rental Housing Board.

Rental Housing Board Chairperson Heaney asked if a Capital Improvement Pass-Through
Fee can be passed down to a property manager who lives in a unit on the property.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson responded that since property manager units are
governed by their employer-employee relationship, Capital Improvement Pass-Through
Fees cannot be passed down to the property manager. Rental Housing Board Liaison
Watson explained that as the employer in an employer-employee relationship, owner has
the ability to revise the employment contract to compensate for the Capital Improvement.
Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that a property manager would not be
categorized as a tenant for purposes of a Capital Improvement Pass-Through Fee.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the Housing Protection Long-Term
Rentals Division proposed four pass-through repayment options for Capital Improvement
petitions. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that the first repayment option
has the longest term with the lowest monthly payment, the second repayment option has
intermediate term with a mid-range monthly payment, the third repayment option has a
shorter term with a higher monthly option, and the fourth repayment option has a customary
term with a monthly payment to be determined by the Rental Housing Board.

Rental Housing Board Member Hamilton asked if the Capital Improvement Pass-Through
Fee is considered rent.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson responded in the affirmative, explaining that the
Inglewood Housing Protection Ordinance No. 21-09 includes pass-through fees in its
definition of rent. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that if tenants do not
pay their pass-through fees, then technically the owner can take the tenant to court.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson ended the presentation by reiterating that the sample
Capital Improvement binder is just a proposal from the Housing Protection Long-Term
Rentals Division. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that if there are any
other factors that the Rental Housing Board Members would like to consider while
evaluating Capital Improvement petitions, then the Housing Protection Long-Term Rentals
Division will be open to that.

  4
 Chairperson Heaney asked if a question could be added that would inquire about the
owner’s previous Capital Improvement compensation from an insurance claim or if the
owner intends to seek compensation from an insurance claim after seeking redress from
the Rental Housing Board.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson replied that the Rental Housing Board Members
have the discretion to make such inquiries. Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson
explained that the Rental Housing Board can require owners to be available at the Capital
Improvement Petition hearings to answer questions from the Rental Housing Board.

The Rental Housing Board Member Hamilton asked if an owner would be eligible to
receive a Capital Improvement Pass-Through fee if the owner had previously been
compensated for their Capital Improvement through an insurance claim.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson explained that if an owner previously received an
insurance reimbursement for the same capital improvement, they would be disqualified.

It was moved by Chairperson Heaney and seconded by Rental Housing Board Hamilton to
add an inquiry to the Capital Improvement Petition that will directly ask the owner if the
owner received compensation from an insurance claim or if the owner intends to seek
compensation from an insurance claim for the capital improvement. The motion was
carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Rental Housing Board Members Hamilton, Fragoso, Brown, and Chairperson
  Heaney;
Noes: None; and
Absent: Rental Housing Board Member Evans.

Rental Housing Board Liaison Watson ended the Capital Improvement presentation by
informing the Rental Housing Board that the Housing Protection Long-Term Rentals
Division is open to any additional feedback that will make processing information more
efficient during the Capital Improvement Petition hearing process.

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING OTHER MATTERS. Chairperson Heaney
inquired if any persons were present who wished to address the Rental Housing Board.

There was no response.

CHAIRPERSON AND BOARD MEMBER REMARKS. Chairperson Heaney inquired
if there were any closing remarks by the Rental Housing Board Members and staff.

There was no response.

There being no further business to be presented, Chairperson Heaney declared the meeting
adjourned at the hour of 3:07 p.m.

  5
 Approved this _____ day of _________, 2025.

Maria Heaney, RHB Chairperson

   CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  HOUSING PROTECTION LONG-TERM RENTALS DIVISION

  OWNER PETITION – FORM A
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PETITION

PURPOSE
An owner should file this form with the Housing Protection Long-Term Rentals Division if there have been capital
improvements to the residential real property that follow the conditions of the Ordinance specified in Section
8-135.
Capital Improvement does not include normal or routine maintenance or repair.
REQUIRED DOCUMENTS
In addition to filing this form, the owner must attach a copy of the Notice of Intent for Capital Improvement
Pass-Through Fee that was delivered to each tenant whose rent would be increased. As well as proof of expenses
made for Capital Improvements.
FOR YOUR INFORMATION
This form becomes a public record when submitted and is subject to disclosure under the California Public
Records Act.
PROCEDURE
An owner may file this form by email, mail or in person. Housing Protection staff will confirm receipt within
three (3) business days of receiving the form.
The Program Administrator will determine if the petition is accepted or denied based on the completeness of
the petition. If the petition is accepted, the Program Administrator will inform the Petitioner about the next
steps. The Program Administrator or designee will schedule the hearing not more than sixty (60) days or less
than fifteen (15) days from when the petition was accepted. The Petitioner and the Responding Party may
showcase any documents, testimony, or other relevant evidence to the petition. This evidence can be submitted
before the hearing, or if needed, evidence can be submitted during the hearing. The Rental Housing Board will
make a determination no later than thirty (30) days after the hearing.

  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT INFORMATION

An owner of residential real property may petition for up to 50% pass-through cost to the tenants to cover
expenses incurred to complete a capital improvement for their property. The applicant shall bear the burden of
establishing that the improvement, addition, or major repair is over $5,000 for a Rental Unit or $10,000 to the
property where the unit is located. Article 4 7 of the Housing Protection Policies and Procedures details the
requirements for a Capital Improvement Petition.

  LETTER OF INTENT FOR CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PASS-THROUGH FEE
Date: ________________________
Dear _________________________________________________________________ [Name of Tenant(s)],

This letter is to inform all tenants residing at _______________________________________________
[Property Address and Unit Number] Inglewood, CA 9030____, that (1) a Capital Improvement project has been
completed at the property listed above, and (2) the property owner has filed a petition with the City of
Inglewood requesting tenant reimbursement of up to 50% of the total capital improvement costs. Under Article
7 of the Housing Protection Policies and Procedures, a Capital Improvement is defined as improvements to a
rental unit or major rehabilitation of a rental unit complex that involves more than ordinary maintenance and
repairs.
TENANT RIGHTS
Capital Improvements must mainly benefit the tenant(s) and be useful for at least five (5) years. These
improvements must also be permanently affixed or relatively immobile and suitable for the intended use of the
rental property.

Capital Improvements do not include the following:

  i.  Normal maintenance and repair, including, repair of a street or driveway.
  ii.  Costs of a replacement that was necessary due to the owner’s failure to carry maintenance
  responsibilities, as determined by the Rental Housing Board.
  iii.  Costs to maintain physical improvements in the common areas or facilities pursuant to California Civil
  Code section 798.15.
  iv.  Additions or replacements made to bring the rental unit into compliance with State or local law, if (1)
  the rental unit has not been in compliance with provisions from the date of its original construction or
  installation, and (2) such provision was in effect at the time of construction or installation.
  v.  Coin-operated improvements or improvements for which a "use fee" or other charge is imposed on
  tenants for their use.

Based upon the circumstances of a particular case, the Rental Housing Board shall have the discretion to
determine capital improvement costs or the appropriate payment over time in any alternative manner
necessary to protect the tenant from excessive rents while ensuring the owner receives a fair return or up to
fifty percent (50%) of the costs.

 What to Expect IF the Capital Improvement Petition is accepted:
  • The Rental Housing Board will hold a hearing to determine the appropriate pass-through amount for the
  tenant, as well as the duration of the pass-through fee.
  • Following the hearing, a 30-day notice will be issued to each tenant, informing them of the final
  determination.
  • Please note, this process may take 3 – 6 months.
 Capital Improvement pass-through fee shall not:

  (a) Exceed $100 per month per rental unit;
  (b) Be more than 72 months;
  (c) Allow the owner to recover more than fifty percent (50%) of the Owner’s Capital Improvement costs; or
  (d) Apply to rental units or new tenants whose initial rent was established after the owner filed the application
  for a pass-through under this section. the completion of the improvement.
